messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate for customer CardinalPay on dedicated cluster ded-nyc-3 (started ~2432109800). 5xx spike, timeouts, increased queue depth. Pager duty: @micah on-call.

micah: on it. paging SRE. any initial impact numbers?

anya: getting graphs now — looks like gateway 502/504s and proxy timeouts to model-proxy. 5xx from 0.2% -> 4.8% over 3 mins. Latency p95 jumped from 120ms -> 1.2s.

ravi: checked pool metrics: ded-nyc-3 GPU utilization at 98% on a subset of servers, queue depth on pool-cardinalpay up 12x. KV cache evictions trending up.

elena: is this noisy neighbor or actual model crash? any OOMs?

anya: no OOMs reported in the runtime logs, but KV eviction rate is high and we see frequent connection resets from the model backend. grabbing logs.

anya: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T15:03:11Z] model-proxy[proxy-12]: upstream error: read tcp 10.2.3.7:443: connection reset by peer
[2026-03-15T15:03:12Z] runtime[runner-7]: kvcache: eviction rate 423/s, miss-rate 18%
[2026-03-15T15:03:13Z] gateway[gw-5]: 502 from upstream model-proxy (timeout)
```

micah: ok, likely noisy tenant within the same pool thrashing KV cache and saturating GPU. need to find culprit session(s). Ravi - can you pull top token counts and active session list for pool-cardinalpay?\
ravi: pulling top sessions now. command i ran:
```bash
redwoodctl sessions list --pool ded-nyc-3 --filter tenant=cardinalpay --top 20 --sort tokens
```

ravi: results show 3 sessions accounting for 72% of active tokens — long-running streaming generations from a single customer key (cid-7321).

anya: good catch. suggest we temporarily throttle that key and enable per-tenant KV isolation policy for the pool. also can we failover CardinalPay to a secondary pool in another region while we mitigate?

elena: we have spare capacity in ded-chi-1 with compatible GPU types. we can shift traffic or create a routing rule to prefer fallback pool.

micah: runbook options: 1) throttle offending API key -> reduces noise; 2) cordon offending servers and drain; 3) shift traffic -> route customer to ded-chi-1 fallback; 4) increase pool capacity (scale up). Do lightweight first: throttle + reroute.

anya: initiating throttle on cid-7321 (rate limit to 5 concurrent streams) now. command:
```bash
redwoodctl quota update --key cid-7321 --concurrency 5 --reason "incident mitigation"
```

deploy-bot: Started update for key cid-7321 (request id f2b3a9).

ravi: throttle applied, seeing immediate drop in token issuance from that key. queue depth decreasing. p95 latency starting to fall.

elena: prepping routing change. creating temporary policy to prefer ded-chi-1 for tenant cardinalpay. will add fallback model variant (redwood-model-quant-lite) if we detect remaining timeouts.

anya: policy snippet:
```json
{"policy": "route_by_tenant", "tenant": "cardinalpay", "preferred_pools": ["ded-chi-1"], "fallback_model": "redwood-model-quant-lite"}
```

micah: roll that policy in when ready. cs-olivia, please notify CardinalPay that we have detected excessive usage from a key and are throttling and routing traffic to mitigate; we'll provide ETA ~20m.

cs-olivia: on it. sending a short note now.

deploy-bot: routing policy applied to tenant cardinalpay (change id rp-9987). health check ongoing.

ravi: after throttle + routing change: 5xx rate down to 0.6%, queue depth back to baseline, p95 ~180ms. KV evictions dropping. GPU saturation reduced to 70% across pool.

anya: still seeing a couple of stale long-running sessions — draining them now from ded-nyc-3. command:
```bash
redwoodctl sessions terminate --pool ded-nyc-3 --session s-9a7b --force
```

elena: cordoned two overloaded hosts and drained tasks. autoscaler added 2 nodes to ded-chi-1 for tail capacity.

micah: thanks team. action summary: throttled offending key cid-7321, applied tenant routing to ded-chi-1, cordoned/drained overloaded hosts, autoscaled fallback pool, notified customer. monitoring for 30m.

cs-olivia: CardinalPay acknowledged and appreciates the update. will keep them posted.

micah: leaving a short post-incident task list: 1) formal noisy-tenant detection rule + auto-throttle (SRE) 2) consider per-tenant KV partitioning (runtime) 3) ITO to review pool sizing and autoscale thresholds (infra) 4) follow-up with CardinalPay about expected request patterns (CS).

anya: adding the above to the incident ticket: INC-2432109876. tagging owners.

micah: marking this thread as monitored — will update when we close. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident condition cleared for ded-nyc-3 (5xx rate normalized). Incident auto-close in 60m if stable.
